source_reasoning: CR1 CSTART is documented read/set: writing zero cannot clear an ongoing transfer. The CSUSP command now masks CSTART out of the sampled control value before writing. It no longer reissues a sampled start1 when asynchronous EOT can clear the actual hardware bit.

The stopped predicate requires sampled CSTART0 and either SUSP or the finite case TSIZE>0 with both EOT and TXC. This accepts normal EOT completion that wins before the suspend command without assuming the hardware must also set SUSP; it does not accept CSTART1 or partial/zero-TSIZE completion evidence.

The model completes the finite hardware event on the second active CR1 read, after drain first observed CSTART1 but before the RMW sample. No simultaneous start1/suspend1 priority is assumed. Actual command values are independently counted before rs zero-write handling; zero writes retain existing CSTART while SPE is enabled.

finish_clock is byte-identical to the old S0.2 function and continues to use independent quiet time after actual idle. Request deadline expiry is not withdrawal proof. Complete submitted RX prefix is drained before SPE clear; CS-high readback precedes owned SCK GPIO handoff and reset. Active frame/caller storage is retained with nonreturn on failed active withdrawal.

Positive timeout race checks original TIMEOUT, count1/RX byte and untouched suffix, no fault callback, actual CS-high/GPIO/reset/quiet ordering, zero SUSP completions and no replayed CSTART. Idle stop positive uses an explicitly trusted pre-existing private owner, not a generated binding or physical test.

Zero TSIZE, EOT-only and TXC-only negatives inspect actual parked subprocess ownership facts. SIGKILL/reap ends only that process; it is not hardware-release evidence. Original33 peripheral source bytes are an exact prefix; old high30 fixture and complete provider header are unchanged. No new mutable provider fields, heap, worker, registry, runtime dispatch or public API was added.
